items.stem: Which statement best defines goodwill?
options: The total of the non-current assets of a business
The amount owed to the business by its customers
The profit earned by a business in its best year
The amount by which the value of a business as a whole exceeds the fair value of its separable net assets
items.answer: The amount by which the value of a business as a whole exceeds the fair value of its separable net assets
items.markingKey: Goodwill = value of business as a whole − fair value of identifiable net assets [1].

items.stem: Explain why goodwill must be valued and adjusted for when a new partner is admitted.
items.answer: Goodwill was built up by the old partners; the new partner will share future profits that partly come from it, so the old partners must be compensated for the share they give up.
items.markingKey: Goodwill created by existing partners [1]; new partner benefits from future profits it generates [1]; adjustment compensates old partners for share sacrificed [1] [3]

items.stem: Explain why many partnerships do not keep a goodwill account in their books after a change in partners.
items.answer: Goodwill is inherent (not purchased); its value is subjective and fluctuates, and IAS 38 does not allow internally generated goodwill to be recognised, so it is written off after the adjustment.
items.markingKey: Subjective/uncertain valuation [1]; internally generated, not purchased [1]; prudence / IAS 38 does not allow recognition [1] [3]

items.stem: The partners of Fjord Fisheries have agreed to value goodwill at 3 years' purchase of the simple average profit. Profits for the last 3 years were: 2021 $113,000, 2022 $122,000, 2023 $123,000. Calculate the value of goodwill.

The partners of Fjord Fisheries have agreed to value goodwill at 2 years' purchase of the weighted average profit (weights 1, 2, 3, 4 with the most recent year weighted highest). Profits for the last 4 years were: 2021 $61,500, 2022 $156,000, 2023 $123,000, 2024 $132,500. Calculate the value of goodwill.

The partners of Kilimanjaro Coffee have agreed to value goodwill at 2.5 years' purchase of the weighted average profit (weights 1, 2, 3, 4 with the most recent year weighted highest). Profits for the last 4 years were: 2021 $78,500, 2022 $95,000, 2023 $48,500, 2024 $127,000. The 2021 profit included a one-off gain of $12,000 on the sale of land, which is not expected to recur. Calculate the value of goodwill.
items.markingKey: Adjust for one-off gain [1]; Σ(profit × weight) = $910,000; ÷ 10 = $91,000 [1]; goodwill = $91,000 × 2.5 = $227,500 [1]

items.stem: The partnership of Mei (capital $58,000) and Aisha (capital $110,000) shares profits and losses 3:1. Arjun joins the firm and brings $37,000 in cash as capital. Premises are revalued upwards by $54,800 and equipment downwards by $6,400; the new values are to be kept. Goodwill is valued at $78,400 but no goodwill account is to remain. The new profit-sharing ratio for Mei, Aisha and Arjun is 2:1:1. (a) Calculate the profit on revaluation and each old partner's share. (b) Explain why Arjun should not receive any share of the revaluation profit.
items.answer: (a) $48,400: Mei $36,300, Aisha $12,100 (b) The increase in value arose before Arjun joined; it belongs to the old partners.
items.markingKey: (a) $54,800 − $6,400 = $48,400 [1]; old ratio 3:1 [1] [2] (b) Gain before admission [1]; old partners entitled [1] [2]

items.stem: The partnership of Isla (capital $73,000) and Diego (capital $72,000) shares profits and losses 3:1. Arjun joins the firm and brings $42,000 in cash as capital. Premises are revalued upwards by $70,000 and equipment downwards by $12,000; the new values are to be kept. Goodwill is valued at $30,000 but no goodwill account is to remain. The new profit-sharing ratio for Isla, Diego and Arjun is 5:4:1. (a) Calculate the profit on revaluation and each old partner's share. (b) Calculate the net goodwill adjustment for each partner.
items.answer: (a) $58,000: Isla $43,500, Diego $14,500 (b) Isla credit $7,500, Diego debit $4,500, Arjun debit $3,000
items.markingKey: (a) $70,000 − $12,000 = $58,000 [1]; old ratio 3:1 [1] [2] (b) Cr old ratio, Dr new ratio [1]; correct nets [2] [3]

items.stem: Distinguish between purchased goodwill and inherent (non-purchased) goodwill.
items.answer: Purchased goodwill arises when one business buys another and pays more than the fair value of its net assets; it can be recorded. Inherent goodwill is built up internally and is not recorded.
items.markingKey: Purchased: paid for on acquisition, recognised [1]; inherent: internally generated, not recognised [1] [2]

items.stem: The partners of Mekong Rice Mills have agreed to value goodwill at 2.5 years' purchase of the weighted average profit (weights 1, 2, 3, 4 with the most recent year weighted highest). Profits for the last 4 years were: 2021 $72,000, 2022 $109,500, 2023 $112,500, 2024 $86,500. The 2024 profit included a one-off gain of $6,500 on the sale of land, which is not expected to recur. Calculate the value of goodwill.
items.markingKey: Adjust for one-off gain [1]; Σ(profit × weight) = $948,500; ÷ 10 = $94,850 [1]; goodwill = $94,850 × 2.5 = $237,125 [1]

items.stem: Complete the statement: On revaluation, an increase in the value of premises is recorded by …
options: debiting premises and crediting the revaluation account
debiting the revaluation account and crediting premises
debiting premises and crediting the new partner's capital
items.answer: debiting premises and crediting the revaluation account
items.markingKey: Increase in asset: Dr asset, Cr revaluation [1].

items.stem: Explain why a revaluation profit is shared in the old profit-sharing ratio and not the new ratio.
items.answer: The change in value occurred while the old partners owned the business, so it belongs to them; using the new ratio would give the incoming partner a share of gains made before he joined.
items.markingKey: Gain earned under old partnership [1]; new partner should not benefit from past gains [1] [2]

items.stem: A partnership decides that the revalued amounts will not be kept in the books. Explain how this is recorded.
items.answer: The revaluation profit/loss is credited to the old partners in the old ratio, then reversed by debiting all partners in the new ratio (a memorandum revaluation), so assets stay at original book values.
items.markingKey: Old partners credited in old ratio [1]; reversed through all partners in new ratio [1]; assets remain at book value [1] [3]

items.stem: Kenji and Ines share profits 2:3. On a change in the profit-sharing ratio the following revaluations were agreed — Premises: increased by $76,000; Equipment: reduced by $11,000; Inventory: written down by $3,500. Calculate the profit or loss on revaluation and each partner's share.
items.answer: Revaluation profit $61,500: Kenji $24,600, Ines $36,900
items.markingKey: Gains: Premises $76,000 ; losses: Equipment $11,000, Inventory $3,500 [1 per 2 items]; net profit $61,500 [1]; shared 2:3 old ratio [1]

items.stem: Chloe and Kwame share profits 7:3. On the retirement of Kwame the following revaluations were agreed — Premises: increased by $40,000; Equipment: reduced by $15,000; Inventory: written down by $1,000; Trade receivables: an allowance for irrecoverable debts of 2% to be created on trade receivables of $28,000; Vehicles: increased by $440. Calculate the profit or loss on revaluation and each partner's share.
items.answer: Revaluation profit $23,880: Chloe $16,716, Kwame $7,164
items.markingKey: Gains: Premises $40,000, Vehicles $440 ; losses: Equipment $15,000, Inventory $1,000, Trade receivables $560 [1 per 2 items]; net profit $23,880 [1]; shared 7:3 old ratio [1]

items.stem: Kilimanjaro Coffee is owned by Grace and Felix, who share profits 3:4 and have capital account balances of $146,000 and $49,000. They admit Kwame, who introduces capital of $34,000 by bank transfer. Premises are revalued upwards by $50,400 and equipment downwards by $6,300; the new values are to be kept. Goodwill is valued at $56,700 but no goodwill account is to remain. The new profit-sharing ratio for Grace, Felix and Kwame is 4:4:1. (a) Calculate the profit on revaluation and each old partner's share. (b) Calculate the net goodwill adjustment for each partner.
items.answer: (a) $44,100: Grace $18,900, Felix $25,200 (b) Grace debit $900, Felix credit $7,200, Kwame debit $6,300
items.markingKey: (a) $50,400 − $6,300 = $44,100 [1]; old ratio 3:4 [1] [2] (b) Cr old ratio, Dr new ratio [1]; correct nets [2] [3]

items.stem: Distinguish between a revaluation account and a realisation account.
items.answer: A revaluation account records changes in asset and liability values when the business continues after a change in partners; a realisation account records the sale of assets and settlement of liabilities when the partnership is dissolved.
items.markingKey: Revaluation: business continues, values change [1]; realisation: business ends, assets sold [1] [2]

items.stem: The partnership of Sofia (capital $129,000) and Omar (capital $108,000) shares profits and losses 3:2. Kwame joins the firm and brings $54,000 in cash as capital. Premises are revalued upwards by $48,000 and equipment downwards by $9,000; the new values are to be kept. Goodwill is valued at $93,000 but no goodwill account is to remain. The new profit-sharing ratio for Sofia, Omar and Kwame is 3:2:1. (a) Calculate the profit on revaluation and each old partner's share. (b) Explain why Kwame should not receive any share of the revaluation profit.
items.answer: (a) $39,000: Sofia $23,400, Omar $15,600 (b) The increase in value arose before Kwame joined; it belongs to the old partners.
items.markingKey: (a) $48,000 − $9,000 = $39,000 [1]; old ratio 3:2 [1] [2] (b) Gain before admission [1]; old partners entitled [1] [2]

items.stem: Complete the statement: A retiring partner is not paid immediately. The balance owed to him should be transferred to …
options: a loan account (shown as a liability)
items.answer: a loan account (shown as a liability)
items.markingKey: Amount due unpaid → retiring partner's loan account [1].

items.stem: Explain why the remaining partners may prefer to pay a retiring partner by instalments through a loan account.
items.answer: Paying in full may drain the bank balance and working capital; a loan spreads the outflow, though interest is payable and it adds gearing.
items.markingKey: Liquidity preserved [1]; interest cost/gearing noted [1] [2]

items.stem: Explain why a partner's capital account and current account are kept separately.
items.answer: Capital accounts show the fixed amount invested; current accounts record the regular items (share of profit, interest, salary, drawings), so fluctuations do not obscure the agreed capital.
items.markingKey: Capital fixed by agreement [1]; current account for appropriation and drawings [1] [2]

items.stem: Ines, Sofia and Mei share profits 3:3:2. Mei retires on 31 May. At that date Mei has a capital balance of $41,000 and a current account credit balance of $11,200. Goodwill is valued at $105,600 (no goodwill account is kept) and a revaluation profit of $7,200 has been calculated. Mei is paid $19,000 in cash and the rest is transferred to a loan account. Calculate the total amount due to Mei and the balance transferred to Mei's loan account.
items.answer: Total due $80,400; loan account $61,400

items.stem: Lina, Chloe and Mohammed share profits 4:3:1. Mohammed retires on 31 May. At that date Mohammed has a capital balance of $37,000 and a current account credit balance of $13,900. Goodwill is valued at $112,800 (no goodwill account is kept) and a revaluation profit of $16,000 has been calculated. Mohammed is paid $27,000 in cash and the rest is transferred to a loan account. Calculate the total amount due to Mohammed and the balance transferred to Mohammed's loan account.
items.answer: Total due $67,000; loan account $40,000

items.stem: Nadia, Ines and Sofia share profits 5:3:2. Sofia retires on 31 May. At that date Sofia has a capital balance of $91,000 and a current account credit balance of $4,300. Goodwill is valued at $41,000 (no goodwill account is kept) and a revaluation profit of $28,000 has been calculated. Sofia is paid $49,000 in cash and the rest is transferred to a loan account. Calculate the total amount due to Sofia and the balance transferred to Sofia's loan account. Nadia and Ines will share future profits 3:2; calculate the net goodwill adjustment to their capital accounts.
items.answer: Due $109,100; loan $60,100; Nadia debit $4,100, Ines debit $4,100

items.stem: The partnership of Isla (capital $140,000) and Grace (capital $104,000) shares profits and losses 1:1. Leila joins the firm and brings $29,000 in cash as capital. Premises are revalued upwards by $36,800 and equipment downwards by $8,000; the new values are to be kept. Goodwill is valued at $77,600 but no goodwill account is to remain. The new profit-sharing ratio for Isla, Grace and Leila is 4:3:1. (a) Calculate the profit on revaluation and each old partner's share. (b) Explain why Leila should not receive any share of the revaluation profit.
items.answer: (a) $28,800: Isla $14,400, Grace $14,400 (b) The increase in value arose before Leila joined; it belongs to the old partners.
items.markingKey: (a) $36,800 − $8,000 = $28,800 [1]; old ratio 1:1 [1] [2] (b) Gain before admission [1]; old partners entitled [1] [2]

items.stem: The partnership of Ana (capital $108,000) and Priya (capital $82,000) shares profits and losses 2:3. Chloe joins the firm and brings $85,000 in cash as capital. Premises are revalued upwards by $54,000 and equipment downwards by $3,000; the new values are to be kept. Goodwill is valued at $102,000 but no goodwill account is to remain. The new profit-sharing ratio for Ana, Priya and Chloe is 3:2:1. (a) Calculate the profit on revaluation and each old partner's share. (b) Calculate the net goodwill adjustment for each partner.
items.answer: (a) $51,000: Ana $20,400, Priya $30,600 (b) Ana debit $10,200, Priya credit $27,200, Chloe debit $17,000
items.markingKey: (a) $54,000 − $3,000 = $51,000 [1]; old ratio 2:3 [1] [2] (b) Cr old ratio, Dr new ratio [1]; correct nets [2] [3]

items.stem: Explain two ways in which the remaining partners could finance the payment to a retiring partner.
items.answer: Introduce extra capital from their own resources; take a bank loan; sell surplus assets; admit a new partner who brings capital.
items.markingKey: Any two methods [1 each] with brief explanation [1 each] [4]

items.stem: Elena and Samuel share profits 2:1. Noah is admitted for a 1/4 share, bringing $63,000 as capital and a cash premium for goodwill. Goodwill of the firm is valued at $136,800; the new ratio is 2:1:1. Calculate (a) the sacrificing ratio, (b) the premium Noah pays and (c) how it is credited to Elena and Samuel.
items.answer: (a) Elena 1/6, Samuel 1/12 (ratio 2:1) (b) $34,200 (c) Elena Cr $22,800, Samuel Cr $11,400

items.stem: Complete the statement: On dissolution, the book value of non-current assets is transferred to the …
options: debit side of the realisation account
credit side of the realisation account
items.answer: debit side of the realisation account
items.markingKey: Dr Realisation, Cr asset accounts [1].

items.stem: Explain the purpose of a realisation account.
items.answer: It records the sale of assets and settlement of liabilities on dissolution, so the profit or loss on realisation can be calculated and shared between the partners in their profit-sharing ratio.
items.markingKey: Records disposal of assets/liabilities [1]; finds profit or loss shared in PSR [1] [2]

items.stem: State two reasons why a partnership may be dissolved.
items.answer: Death, retirement or bankruptcy of a partner; expiry of an agreed term; disagreement between partners; business no longer profitable; court order.
items.markingKey: Any two [1 each] [2]

items.stem: Jonas and Aisha dissolved their partnership, in which they shared profits 2:3. Non-current assets (book value $119,000) were sold for $141,300; inventory (book value $26,500) sold for $20,700; trade receivables of $10,300 collected $9,700; trade payables of $7,600 were settled for $7,500; dissolution expenses were $500. Calculate the profit or loss on realisation and each partner's share.
items.answer: Realisation profit $15,500: Jonas $6,200, Aisha $9,300
items.markingKey: Dr side: assets at book value $155,800 + expenses $500 [1]; Cr side: proceeds $171,700 + discount on payables $100 [1]; profit $15,500 [1]; shares Jonas $6,200, Aisha $9,300 [1]

items.stem: Samuel and Jonas dissolved their partnership, in which they shared profits 2:3. Non-current assets (book value $160,000) were sold for $189,500; inventory (book value $10,500) sold for $8,600; trade receivables of $13,700 collected $12,500; Samuel took over a vehicle with a book value of $8,000 at an agreed value of $5,000; trade payables of $7,700 were settled for $7,000; dissolution expenses were $1,600. Calculate the profit or loss on realisation and each partner's share.
items.answer: Realisation profit $22,500: Samuel $9,000, Jonas $13,500
items.markingKey: Dr side: assets at book value $192,200 + expenses $1,600 [1]; Cr side: proceeds $210,600 + asset taken over $5,000 + discount on payables $700 [1]; profit $22,500 [1]; shares Samuel $9,000, Jonas $13,500 [1]

items.stem: Elena and Aisha, sharing profits 7:3, dissolve their partnership. Their statement of financial position shows: non-current assets $79,000 (including a car at $4,500), inventory $27,600, trade receivables $15,900, bank $5,000, trade payables $6,000, capital Elena $89,500, capital Aisha $32,000. Other non-current assets were sold for $89,200, inventory for $24,400 and receivables realised $15,400. Elena took the car at $6,500. Payables accepted $5,300 in full settlement and dissolution costs were $2,700. (a) Calculate the amount paid to each partner to close the business. (b) Explain why the car taken over by a partner is credited to the realisation account.
items.answer: (a) Elena $90,700, Aisha $35,300 (b) It is treated as if sold to the partner at the agreed value; the partner's capital is debited instead of cash received.

items.stem: Daniel and Ethan dissolved their partnership, in which they shared profits 4:1. Non-current assets (book value $141,000) were sold for $176,000; inventory (book value $30,200) sold for $24,200; trade receivables of $19,400 collected $17,400; dissolution expenses were $4,000. What is the profit (loss) on realisation?
items.markingKey: Dr side: assets at book value $190,600 + expenses $4,000 [1]; Cr side: proceeds $217,600 [1]; profit $23,000 [1]; shares Daniel $18,400, Ethan $4,600 [1]

items.stem: Complete the statement: When a partnership is converted into a limited company, the purchase consideration is credited to the …
options: share premium account of the partnership
items.answer: realisation account
items.markingKey: Dr Company (purchaser) account, Cr Realisation with purchase consideration [1].

items.stem: Complete the statement: Shares received from the new company are distributed to the partners …
options: in the ratio of their drawings
in the ratio agreed (often their final capital balances)
items.answer: in the ratio agreed (often their final capital balances)
items.markingKey: Shares are allotted by agreement, normally to settle closing capital balances [1].

items.stem: Explain one advantage and one disadvantage to the partners of converting their business into a limited company.
items.answer: Advantage: limited liability / easier to raise capital by selling shares. Disadvantage: loss of privacy (accounts published), more regulation and cost, possible loss of control.
items.markingKey: Advantage with reason [1+1]; disadvantage with reason [1+1] [4]

items.stem: Cobalt Ltd was formed to take over the partnership of Lina and Tomás. All assets and liabilities were taken over; their book value was $188,000 and the agreed fair value was $228,000. The purchase consideration was 250,000 ordinary shares of $1 each issued at $1.50 per share plus $10,000 in cash. Calculate the purchase consideration and the goodwill recognised by Cobalt Ltd.
items.answer: Consideration $385,000; goodwill $157,000

items.stem: Leila and Felix share profits 3:4. Their partnership is taken over by Galaxy Ltd. Book values: non-current assets $242,000, current assets $114,000, current liabilities $40,000; capitals Leila $115,000, Felix $201,000. Galaxy Ltd values the non-current assets at $286,000 and other items at book value. The consideration is 190,000 ordinary shares of $1 issued at $2.00 each and $24,200 in cash. Calculate the profit on realisation and each partner's share.
items.markingKey: Consideration $404,200 − net assets $316,000 = $88,200 [2]; shared 3:4 [1] [3]

items.stem: In which part of a statement of financial position would purchased goodwill be shown?
items.answer: Intangible non-current assets
items.markingKey: Purchased goodwill is an intangible non-current asset [1].

items.stem: State and explain two limitations of valuing goodwill on the basis of past average profits.
items.answer: Past profits may not be repeated in future (e.g. key partner leaving, new competition); profits may include one-off items that distort the average.
items.markingKey: Past not a guide to future [1] + reason [1]; abnormal items distort average [1] + reason [1] [4]

items.stem: Aurora Printing is owned by 2 partners. Average annual profits are $175,000 and capital employed is $540,000. A normal return on capital in this industry is 6% and the partners could each earn $27,000 a year in employment elsewhere. Goodwill is to be valued at 3 years' purchase of super profits. Calculate the value of goodwill.

Chloe, Diego and Leila share profits 3:2:1 in Mekong Rice Mills. Capital balances (after current accounts have been transferred) are Chloe $114,000, Diego $34,000 and Leila $91,000. Leila retires. Goodwill is valued at $75,600 (no goodwill account is kept) and the revaluation profit is $19,200. Leila receives $32,000 immediately; the balance is left as a loan at 6% interest. Chloe and Diego will share profits 3:1. (a) Calculate the net goodwill adjustment to the capital accounts of Chloe and Diego. (b) Explain how the loan to Leila will be presented in the statement of financial position.
items.answer: (a) Chloe debit $18,900; Diego credit $6,300 (b) As a liability: non-current if repayable after 12 months, current for any instalment due within 12 months.
items.markingKey: (a) Cr old ratio, Dr new ratio 3:1 [1]; Chloe debit $18,900 [1]; Diego credit $6,300 [1] [3] (b) Liability [1]; current/non-current split [1] [2]

items.stem: Answer both parts. (a) Complete the statement: On revaluation, an increase in the value of premises is recorded by … (b) Complete the statement: Creating an allowance for irrecoverable debts on revaluation will …
items.answer: (a) debiting premises and crediting the revaluation account (b) reduce the revaluation profit
items.markingKey: (a) Increase in asset: Dr asset, Cr revaluation [1]. (b) Dr revaluation, Cr allowance: a loss on revaluation [1].

items.stem: Aisha, Chloe and Isla share profits 3:3:2. On the retirement of Isla the following revaluations were agreed — Premises: increased by $75,200; Equipment: reduced by $12,800; Inventory: written down by $2,400. Calculate the profit or loss on revaluation and each partner's share.
items.answer: Revaluation profit $60,000: Aisha $22,500, Chloe $22,500, Isla $15,000
items.markingKey: Gains: Premises $75,200 ; losses: Equipment $12,800, Inventory $2,400 [1 per 2 items]; net profit $60,000 [1]; shared 3:3:2 old ratio [1]

items.stem: Pacific Tiles is owned by Ines and Grace, who share profits 2:3 and have capital account balances of $58,000 and $96,000. They admit Felix, who introduces capital of $50,000 by bank transfer. Premises are revalued upwards by $24,000 and equipment downwards by $12,000; the new values are to be kept. Goodwill is valued at $36,000 but no goodwill account is to remain. The new profit-sharing ratio for Ines, Grace and Felix is 3:3:2. (a) Calculate the profit on revaluation and each old partner's share. (b) Explain why Felix should not receive any share of the revaluation profit.
items.answer: (a) $12,000: Ines $4,800, Grace $7,200 (b) The increase in value arose before Felix joined; it belongs to the old partners.
items.markingKey: (a) $24,000 − $12,000 = $12,000 [1]; old ratio 2:3 [1] [2] (b) Gain before admission [1]; old partners entitled [1] [2]

items.stem: Give a reason for each answer. (a) Explain why a partner's capital account and current account are kept separately. (b) Explain why the remaining partners may prefer to pay a retiring partner by instalments through a loan account.
items.answer: (a) Capital accounts show the fixed amount invested; current accounts record the regular items (share of profit, interest, salary, drawings), so fluctuations do not obscure the agreed capital. (b) Paying in full may drain the bank balance and working capital; a loan spreads the outflow, though interest is payable and it adds gearing.
items.markingKey: (a) Capital fixed by agreement [1]; current account for appropriation and drawings [1] [2] (b) Liquidity preserved [1]; interest cost/gearing noted [1] [2]

items.stem: Give a reason for each answer. (a) Explain two ways in which the remaining partners could finance the payment to a retiring partner. (b) Explain why the remaining partners may prefer to pay a retiring partner by instalments through a loan account.
items.answer: (a) Introduce extra capital from their own resources; take a bank loan; sell surplus assets; admit a new partner who brings capital. (b) Paying in full may drain the bank balance and working capital; a loan spreads the outflow, though interest is payable and it adds gearing.
items.markingKey: (a) Any two methods [1 each] with brief explanation [1 each] [4] (b) Liquidity preserved [1]; interest cost/gearing noted [1] [2]

items.stem: Aisha and Noah share profits 7:3. Isla is admitted for a 1/10 share, bringing $58,000 as capital and a cash premium for goodwill. Goodwill of the firm is valued at $59,000; the new ratio is 6:3:1. Calculate (a) the sacrificing ratio, (b) the premium Isla pays and (c) how it is credited to Aisha and Noah.
items.answer: (a) Aisha 1/10, Noah 0 (ratio all Aisha) (b) $5,900 (c) Aisha Cr $5,900, Noah Cr $0

items.stem: Explain why the bank account and cash are not transferred to the realisation account on dissolution.
items.answer: Cash is not "realised" — it is already in money form and is used to pay liabilities and partners, so it stays in the bank account.
items.markingKey: Cash already realised [1]; used to settle with creditors/partners [1] [2]

items.stem: Isla and Lina dissolved their partnership, in which they shared profits 2:1. Non-current assets (book value $62,000) were sold for $75,200; inventory (book value $35,400) sold for $31,600; trade receivables of $29,800 collected $27,800; trade payables of $20,800 were settled for $20,100; dissolution expenses were $2,400. Calculate the profit or loss on realisation and each partner's share.
items.answer: Realisation profit $5,700: Isla $3,800, Lina $1,900
items.markingKey: Dr side: assets at book value $127,200 + expenses $2,400 [1]; Cr side: proceeds $134,600 + discount on payables $700 [1]; profit $5,700 [1]; shares Isla $3,800, Lina $1,900 [1]

items.stem: Hana and Samuel, sharing profits 4:1, dissolve their partnership. Their statement of financial position shows: non-current assets $73,000 (including a car at $11,000), inventory $21,000, trade receivables $14,800, bank $52,200, trade payables $8,000, capital Hana $67,000, capital Samuel $86,000. Other non-current assets were sold for $90,000, inventory for $19,700 and receivables realised $13,300. Hana took the car at $12,000. Payables accepted $6,900 in full settlement and dissolution costs were $2,800. (a) Calculate the amount paid to each partner to close the business. (b) Explain why the car taken over by a partner is credited to the realisation account.
items.answer: (a) Hana $74,600, Samuel $90,900 (b) It is treated as if sold to the partner at the agreed value; the partner's capital is debited instead of cash received.

items.stem: Explain why goodwill may appear in the new company's statement of financial position after a partnership is converted.
items.answer: If the purchase consideration exceeds the fair value of net assets taken over, the excess is purchased goodwill, which the company can recognise as an intangible asset.
items.markingKey: Consideration > fair value of net assets [1]; purchased goodwill recognised [1] [2]

items.stem: Sirocco plc was formed to take over the partnership of Noah and Aisha. All assets and liabilities were taken over; their book value was $223,000 and the agreed fair value was $267,000. The purchase consideration was 240,000 ordinary shares of $1 each issued at $1.25 per share plus $63,000 in cash. Calculate (a) the purchase consideration, (b) the goodwill in Sirocco plc's books, (c) the share premium created and (d) the profit on realisation in the partnership books.
Complete the statement: A partnership does not keep a goodwill account. On admission of a new partner, goodwill is first credited to the old partners in their …
items.answer: old profit-sharing ratio
items.markingKey: Create goodwill: Dr Goodwill, Cr old partners in OLD ratio; write off: Cr Goodwill, Dr all partners in NEW ratio [1].

items.stem: Explain why goodwill is written off in the new profit-sharing ratio after being credited in the old ratio.
items.answer: Crediting in the old ratio rewards the partners who built it; debiting in the new ratio charges all partners who now share its future benefit, so the net effect transfers value from gaining to sacrificing partners.
items.markingKey: Old ratio rewards creators [1]; new ratio charges future beneficiaries [1]; net effect = sacrifice/gain [1] [3]

items.stem: Harbour Electrics is owned by 3 partners. Average annual profits are $205,000 and capital employed is $420,000. A normal return on capital in this industry is 10% and the partners could each earn $25,000 a year in employment elsewhere. Goodwill is to be valued at 3 years' purchase of super profits. Calculate the value of goodwill.

Omar and Elena are in partnership trading as Harbour Electrics, sharing profits 2:1. Their capital balances are Omar $40,000 and Elena $72,000. On 1 April Lucas is admitted, paying $79,000 into the business bank account as capital. Premises are revalued upwards by $79,200 and equipment downwards by $12,000; the new values are to be kept. Goodwill is valued at $139,200 but no goodwill account is to remain. The new profit-sharing ratio for Omar, Elena and Lucas is 3:3:2. (a) Calculate the net goodwill adjustment for each partner. (b) Explain why Lucas should not receive any share of the revaluation profit.
items.answer: (a) Omar credit $40,600, Elena debit $5,800, Lucas debit $34,800 (b) The increase in value arose before Lucas joined; it belongs to the old partners.
items.markingKey: (a) Cr old ratio, Dr new ratio [1]; correct nets [2] [3] (b) Gain before admission [1]; old partners entitled [1] [2]

items.stem: Answer both parts. (a) Complete the statement: A profit on revaluation is shared between the partners in … (b) Which account is closed by transferring its balance to the partners' capital accounts?
items.answer: (a) the old profit-sharing ratio (b) Revaluation account
items.markingKey: (a) The gain arose while the old partnership existed, so old ratio [1]. (b) Revaluation profit/loss is transferred to capitals in old ratio [1].

items.stem: Hana and Diego share profits 3:1. On the retirement of Diego the following revaluations were agreed — Premises: increased by $43,200; Equipment: reduced by $8,000; Inventory: written down by $6,000. Calculate the profit or loss on revaluation and each partner's share.
items.answer: Revaluation profit $29,200: Hana $21,900, Diego $7,300
items.markingKey: Gains: Premises $43,200 ; losses: Equipment $8,000, Inventory $6,000 [1 per 2 items]; net profit $29,200 [1]; shared 3:1 old ratio [1]

items.stem: The partnership of Felix (capital $115,000) and Lina (capital $56,000) shares profits and losses 2:1. Chloe joins the firm and brings $68,000 in cash as capital. Premises are revalued upwards by $36,300 and equipment downwards by $4,200; the new values are to be kept. Goodwill is valued at $39,900 but no goodwill account is to remain. The new profit-sharing ratio for Felix, Lina and Chloe is 1:1:1. (a) Calculate the profit on revaluation and each old partner's share. (b) Explain why Chloe should not receive any share of the revaluation profit.
items.answer: (a) $32,100: Felix $21,400, Lina $10,700 (b) The increase in value arose before Chloe joined; it belongs to the old partners.
items.markingKey: (a) $36,300 − $4,200 = $32,100 [1]; old ratio 2:1 [1] [2] (b) Gain before admission [1]; old partners entitled [1] [2]

items.stem: Answer both parts. (a) Explain two ways in which the remaining partners could finance the payment to a retiring partner. (b) Explain why a partner's capital account and current account are kept separately.
items.answer: (a) Introduce extra capital from their own resources; take a bank loan; sell surplus assets; admit a new partner who brings capital. (b) Capital accounts show the fixed amount invested; current accounts record the regular items (share of profit, interest, salary, drawings), so fluctuations do not obscure the agreed capital.
items.markingKey: (a) Any two methods [1 each] with brief explanation [1 each] [4] (b) Capital fixed by agreement [1]; current account for appropriation and drawings [1] [2]

items.stem: Give a reason for each answer. (a) Explain why a partner's capital account and current account are kept separately. (b) Explain two ways in which the remaining partners could finance the payment to a retiring partner.
items.answer: (a) Capital accounts show the fixed amount invested; current accounts record the regular items (share of profit, interest, salary, drawings), so fluctuations do not obscure the agreed capital. (b) Introduce extra capital from their own resources; take a bank loan; sell surplus assets; admit a new partner who brings capital.
items.markingKey: (a) Capital fixed by agreement [1]; current account for appropriation and drawings [1] [2] (b) Any two methods [1 each] with brief explanation [1 each] [4]

items.stem: Zara, Jonas and Yusuf share profits 5:4:1. Yusuf retires on 31 May. At that date Yusuf has a capital balance of $67,000 and a current account credit balance of $11,800. Goodwill is valued at $133,000 (no goodwill account is kept) and a revaluation profit of $40,000 has been calculated. Yusuf is paid $44,000 in cash and the rest is transferred to a loan account. Calculate the total amount due to Yusuf and the balance transferred to Yusuf's loan account.
items.answer: Total due $96,100; loan account $52,100

items.stem: On the dissolution of the partnership of Mateo and Kenji, Mateo took over office equipment with a book value of $7,000 at an agreed value of $10,500. The bookkeeper debited the realisation account and credited Mateo's capital account with $10,500. Explain the error and its effect on the amount paid to Mateo.
items.answer: The entry is reversed: Mateo's capital should be debited (he receives an asset instead of cash) and realisation credited. The error overstates Mateo's capital by $21,000 before sharing, so he would be overpaid.
items.markingKey: Correct entry Dr capital Mateo, Cr realisation [1]; reason asset received in lieu of cash [1]; effect: capital overstated by 2 × $10,500 = $21,000 (before realisation result) [1] [3]

items.stem: Ravi and Tomás dissolved their partnership, in which they shared profits 3:2. Non-current assets (book value $83,000) were sold for $89,600; inventory (book value $13,500) sold for $11,300; trade receivables of $20,600 collected $18,900; trade payables of $19,800 were settled for $19,400; dissolution expenses were $1,100. Calculate the profit or loss on realisation and each partner's share.
items.answer: Realisation profit $2,000: Ravi $1,200, Tomás $800
items.markingKey: Dr side: assets at book value $117,100 + expenses $1,100 [1]; Cr side: proceeds $119,800 + discount on payables $400 [1]; profit $2,000 [1]; shares Ravi $1,200, Tomás $800 [1]

items.stem: Mateo and Diego, sharing profits 3:1, dissolve their partnership. Their statement of financial position shows: non-current assets $150,000 (including a car at $5,000), inventory $14,200, trade receivables $23,300, bank $9,000, trade payables $17,600, capital Mateo $113,900, capital Diego $65,000. Other non-current assets were sold for $150,700, inventory for $12,200 and receivables realised $21,400. Mateo took the car at $6,000. Payables accepted $16,700 in full settlement and dissolution costs were $2,500. (a) Calculate the amount paid to each partner to close the business. (b) Explain why the car taken over by a partner is credited to the realisation account.
items.answer: (a) Mateo $108,800, Diego $65,300 (b) It is treated as if sold to the partner at the agreed value; the partner's capital is debited instead of cash received.

items.stem: When Tamarind Ltd took over the partnership of Aisha and Mei, it issued 120,000 ordinary shares of $1 at $1.75. The company accountant credited the whole $210,000 to the ordinary share capital account. Explain the error and state the correct entries.
items.answer: Share capital must show nominal value only: Cr ordinary share capital $120,000; the excess $90,000 is credited to share premium.
items.markingKey: Share capital at nominal value [1]; share capital $120,000 [1]; share premium $90,000 [1] [3]

items.stem: Condor Ltd was formed to take over the partnership of Ethan and Ines. All assets and liabilities were taken over; their book value was $208,000 and the agreed fair value was $237,000. The purchase consideration was 180,000 ordinary shares of $1 each issued at $1.60 per share plus $71,000 in cash. Calculate (a) the purchase consideration, (b) the goodwill in Condor Ltd's books, (c) the share premium created and (d) the profit on realisation in the partnership books.
